The test image shows a corn ear with massive black powdery/spore masses replacing the normal ear structure, with dried/torn husks. The affected part is the pod/ear. From the part index, pod candidates are: Head_Smut, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Tar_Spot, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma.

The black spore masses strongly point to Head_Smut. Let me confirm with one reference.

The reference Head_Smut image matches the test image very well: dark brown-black spore masses filling the ear cavity with dried husks pulled back. Both show the ear structure completely replaced by spore masses.

The test image features:
- Corn ear/pod affected
- Massive black spore masses replacing normal ear tissue
- Dried, torn husks exposing the spore mass
- No normal kernels visible

This matches Head_Smut perfectly: "Large smut galls replace ears... rupture to release masses of dark brown spores... teardrop-shaped ears lacking silks with husks filled with teliospores."
